South-East Asia Payment Firms Raise US$1.6 Billion
By Minjun Park
2 min read Updated Nov 24, 2026 Publication date: Nov 24, 2026 4:49 AM
Share | Save

Questions & Answers
Which deals drove the surge in South-east Asian payment funding?
Why did early-stage funding figures increase so dramatically?
How is payment sector investment distributed geographically across the region?
What does the typical exit path look like for payment firms in the region?
Why it matters
South-east Asian payment firms secured US$1.6 billion by mid-November 2026, driven almost entirely by mega-rounds for Ant International and Airwallex.
Capital concentration in Singapore starves early-stage regional fintechs, with deal counts collapsing to 10 and seed transactions tumbling from nine to one.
Track whether local champions like Xendit and MoMo can unlock liquidity, given trade sales average an extended 19.5 years to reach US$80.9 million.
Retail News Asia newsroom analysis
South-east Asia’s payment companies raised US$1.6 billion in equity funding between Jan 1 and Nov 17, 2026. That total more than doubles the US$733 million secured across the entire twelve months of 2025.
The capital injection represents the highest annual funding level for the sector since 2022. It extends a three-year recovery from 2023, when sector investment hit a trough of US$270 million. Capital flow, however, concentrated heavily into a tiny cluster of mega-transactions rather than a broad market expansion.
Mega-rounds skew early-stage totals
Two transactions accounted for the vast majority of the capital raised across the region this year. Ant International secured US$1.2 billion in a Series A round in July, while cross-border payments provider Airwallex closed a US$320 million Series H round in June.

Because Ant International structured its transaction as a Series A round, early-stage capital metrics surged to US$1.3 billion for the year. Late-stage funding reached just US$320 million through mid-November. The breakdown reverses the distribution recorded in 2025, when late-stage financing rounds comprised US$662 million of the US$733 million raised.
Deal volumes fall across the region
Underlying deal activity contracted sharply despite the top-line dollar expansion. Investors completed only 10 equity deals across South-east Asia through Nov 17, 2026.
Early-stage venture creation experienced the steepest drop. Seed rounds fell from nine completed transactions in 2025 to a single deal in 2026. The compression leaves early-stage fintech founders facing a substantially narrower base of active institutional checks than in prior fundraising cycles.
Singapore captures the bulk of capital
Geographic allocation remains skewed toward Singapore, which drew approximately 71.1 per cent of all payment sector funding in South-east Asia. The city-state has payment unicorns Airwallex, Coda, and cross-border infrastructure network Thunes.
Thunes represents the most recent addition to the regional unicorn roster, having crossed the US$1 billion valuation mark in April 2025. Other markets maintain discrete domestic champions: Thailand houses Omise and Ascend Money, Indonesia supports Xendit, the Philippines counts GCash and Voyager Innovations, and Vietnam includes MoMo and VNPay.
Trade sales dominate liquidity events
Trade acquisitions continue to serve as the primary route to liquidity for investors and founders in the region. South-east Asia has logged 53 acquisitions and nine initial public offerings in the payments vertical to date.
The path to an acquisition remains extended. Payment firms averaged 19.5 years from their initial funding round to an acquisition, securing an average transaction price of US$80.9 million. Corporate buyers completed two acquisitions in 2026 through Nov 17, compared with three in 2025, while public listings remained flat with one IPO completed in each year.
What this means
Headline funding gains mask a severe liquidity crunch for South-east Asian fintech. Funnelling capital into Ant International and Airwallex creates an unsustainable divide. This lopsided backing directly pressures regional champions like Xendit, GCash, and MoMo, which must now defend domestic turf without comparable mega-checks. While Thunes secured a unicorn valuation in April 2025, newer entrants face a closed door after seed activity collapsed to a solitary round. The core risk is an innovation drought across peripheral markets as Singapore monopolises institutional dry powder. Watch whether corporate acquirers surpass the US$80.9 million average exit price before year-end.

Congo mining forum announces $965 million in sector financing
The financing will support small and medium-sized enterprises, mining subcontracting and local processing of resources.
Reuters
|
November 24, 2026 - 3:51 pm
Categories:
Exploration
Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo. Stock image.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo will receive $965 million in mining-sector investment, organizers announced at the opening of the Makutano Mining Forum in Kinshasa.
Of that total, $700 million is earmarked for financing in the Congolese mining sector, with financial institutions committing to support the sector and its entire value chain.
The remaining $265 million is being provided through the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to support the private sector in the DRC.
The financing will support small and medium-sized enterprises, mining subcontracting, local processing of resources and trade finance.
President Felix Tshisekedi used the opening ceremony to reaffirm the DRC’s aim to move beyond extracting resources to creating added value through local processing, saying this would bring “lasting prosperity for the people.”
(Reporting by Congo newsroom. Editing by Ayen Deng Bior and Mark Potter)

Credit Acceptance Announces Completion of $800.0 Million Asset-Backed Financing
by GlobeNewswire
Nov 25, 2026 5:13 am
Southfield, Michigan, Nov. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Credit Acceptance Corporation (Nasdaq: CACC) (referred to as the "Company”, "Credit Acceptance”, "we”, "our”, or "us”) announced today the completion of an $800.0 million asset-backed non-recourse secured financing (the "Financing”). Pursuant to this transaction, we conveyed loans having a value of approximately $1.0 billion to a wholly owned special purpose entity which will transfer the loans to a trust, which will issue three classes of notes:
Note Class Amount Average Life Price Interest Rate
A $ 397,334,000 2.49 years 99.97736% 5.73%
B $ 158,400,000 3.15 years 99.99401% 6.01%
C $ 244,266,000 3.65 years 99.99546% 6.27% The Financing will:
have an expected average annualized cost of approximately 6.2% including upfront fees and other costs;
revolve for 24 months after which it will amortize based upon the cash flows on the conveyed loans; and
be used by us to repay higher cost outstanding indebtedness and for general corporate purposes. We will receive 4.0% of the cash flows related to the underlying consumer loans to cover servicing expenses. The remaining 96.0%, less amounts due to dealers for payments of dealer holdback, will be used to pay principal and interest on the notes as well as the ongoing costs of the Financing. The Financing is structured so as not to affect our contractual relationships with dealers and to preserve the dealers’ rights to future payments of dealer holdback.
Following the completion of this financing, Credit Acceptance maintained approximately $1.5 billion in unused and available borrowing capacity on its revolving credit facilities and unrestricted cash. "Completing our largest securitization to date is an important milestone for our diversified funding strategy,” said Jay Brinkley, Treasurer of Credit Acceptance. "The transaction reflects continued investor support for our ABS program and demonstrates our ability to access the capital markets at meaningful scale.”
The notes have not been and will not be registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration requirements. This news release does not and will not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy the notes. This news release is being issued pursuant to and in accordance with Rule 135c under the Securities Act of 1933.
Description of Credit Acceptance Corporation
We make vehicle ownership possible by providing innovative financing solutions that enable automobile dealers to sell vehicles to consumers regardless of their credit history. Our financing programs are offered through a nationwide network of automobile dealers who benefit from sales of vehicles to consumers who otherwise could not obtain financing; from repeat and referral sales generated by these same customers; and from sales to customers responding to advertisements for our financing programs, but who actually end up qualifying for traditional financing.
Without our financing programs, consumers are often unable to purchase vehicles, or they purchase unreliable ones. Further, as we report to the three national credit reporting agencies, an important ancillary benefit of our programs is that we provide consumers with an opportunity to improve their lives by improving their credit score and move on to more traditional sources of financing. Credit Acceptance is publicly traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the symbol CACC. For more information, visit creditacceptance.com .

candidates.title: Accel Leads a $277 Million Seed Round for Marlowe, Valuing the Non-Nvidia AI Inference Startup at $1.15 Billion
candidates.snippet: Accel Leads a $277 Million Seed Round for Marlowe, Valuing the Non-Nvidia AI Inference Startup at $1.15 Billion HedgeCo.Net
candidates.text:
Marlowe, an AI infrastructure startup founded in May by Convoy co-founder Dan Lewis and former Microsoft corporate vice president Kutta Srinivasan, has raised a $277 million seed round led by Accel. The financing values the company at $1.15 billion, according to the company as reported by GeekWire, making it a unicorn at the seed stage.
Marlowe said its seed investors include Accel, Bessemer, Altimeter, Atreides, Eclipse, Journey, Valor, Emergence Capital, Pitango and Neo, among others. Quartz, citing Bloomberg, reported that Eclipse had led an earlier round and that Eclipse chief executive Lior Susan serves as Marlowe’s executive chairman. GeekWire noted angel backers including KKR co-founder Henry Kravis and Uber chief executive Dara Khosrowshahi.
The company is building what it calls multi-silicon AI factories: data centers designed specifically for inference workloads and built around chips from vendors other than Nvidia, starting with AMD and the startup Etched. Marlowe argues that co-designing chips, networking, power management and software can deliver two to three times more output per watt and per dollar than conventional GPU clouds. GeekWire reported that its first site, built around Etched chips, is scheduled to go live in December, with a larger AMD-based site targeted for the second quarter of 2027.
The size of the round reflects how capital-intensive AI infrastructure has become even at the earliest stage. The founders told GeekWire that much of the money will go toward chips, networking equipment and site operations, and that the company plans to prove its approach at sites of tens of megawatts before financing additional capacity site by site.
For venture investors, Marlowe is a bet that the shift from training models to running them will open room for alternatives to Nvidia’s dominant ecosystem. It also highlights a broader trend of seed rounds that look more like growth financings, which concentrates risk in fewer companies and raises the bar for follow-on rounds. Execution on the first two sites will be the key test of whether the valuation holds.

Peak Energy Expands Series B Total Financing to $157 Million to Accelerate Manufacturing Amid Growing Customer Backlog
News provided by
Peak Energy Technologies
Nov 24, 2026, 11:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Additional capital will support U.S. manufacturing expansion and commercial deployments beginning in 2027
BURLINGAME, Calif. , Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Peak Energy , the leading developer of passively cooled sodium-ion energy storage systems for the grid, today announced it has expanded its Series B financing to $157 million, including $132 million in equity financing and a $25 million debt facility from HSBC. The additional capital will accelerate manufacturing capacity to meet growing customer demand and support commercial deployments beginning in 2027.
"Customers are telling us they need a lot more energy storage, and they need better options," said Landon Mossburg, co-founder and CEO of Peak Energy. "That's especially true as data centers drive a new wave of electricity demand. We built Peak to solve the economics of storage at scale, but also to build systems that are easier to live with: quieter, simpler and safer. This capital lets us move faster on both."
Peak initially announced its oversubscribed Series B in October, led by General Motors Ventures with participation from Maverick Silicon, Infinite Capital, Eclipse, Xora Innovation and LG Technology Ventures. With more than $2.5 billion in customer agreements and growing commercial momentum, Peak expanded the round in response to additional investor interest. The new investment will accelerate the company's manufacturing buildout and support a pilot project demonstrating the long-term economic benefits of Peak's technology for data centers. The $25 million HSBC facility will support project deliveries beginning in 2027 and help Peak scale its supply chain as commercial production ramps.
"We're grateful to our existing investors for deepening their support as our backlog grows," said Zack Jacobson, Vice President of Finance at Peak Energy. "Adding HSBC gives us flexibility to fund project deliveries without additional dilution and reserve equity for scaling the business. Building a capital stack that fits each need is how we'll finance Peak's growth, and HSBC is the right partner to lead that."
Peak's flagship passively cooled energy storage system eliminates active cooling systems, requires zero planned maintenance and can reduce the cost of energy by up to 20% compared with conventional storage systems. With systems designed to perform for 30 years without augmentation, Peak delivers significant long-term economic benefits for customers, including data centers with large and growing power needs.
To learn more about Peak Energy, visit peakenergy.com .
ABOUT PEAK ENERGY:
Peak Energy is a U.S.-based company building sodium-ion energy storage to solve today's grid infrastructure challenges. With $157 million in new financing, Peak is ramping domestic manufacturing at its 4 GWh facility in Sacramento, California, to meet growing demand for U.S.-made energy storage. Founded in 2023, the company has over $2.5 billion in commercial agreements, including deals with Jupiter Power, RWE, and Energy Vault, and a strategic partnership with General Motors to develop next-generation storage cells purpose-built for the grid. Built by veterans from Tesla, Enovix, and Fluence, Peak's proprietary passive cooling platform makes grid-scale storage safer, simpler, and more affordable. For more information, visit www.peakenergy.com .

[email protected]

Chase Properties and Tru Arrow Partners Raise More Than $148 Million Across Two Real Estate Funds
November 24, 2026
Creekside Plaza in Ithaca, N.Y., one of the open-air shopping centers acquired by Fund V alongside TACPP. (Photo: Chase Properties)
Chase Properties , a Beachwood, Ohio-based owner and operator of open-air shopping centers, and New York-based alternative asset manager Tru Arrow Partners have completed the final closings of two real estate investment funds, securing more than $148 million in combined capital commitments.
Tru Arrow-Chase Properties Partners (TACPP) closed at nearly $105 million, while Chase Properties Retail Opportunities Fund V closed at nearly $44 million. Both funds closed within their respective fundraising targets.
Fund V follows a core-plus investment strategy focused on stabilized, income-producing shopping centers, while TACPP pursues opportunistic investments across retail, multifamily and industrial properties, including investments alongside Chase Properties’ retail funds.
Fund V has acquired eight open-air shopping centers alongside TACPP across New York, Virginia, Arkansas, Texas and Illinois, with a ninth property currently under contract.
The portfolio includes prominent national retailers such as T.J. Maxx, HomeGoods, Ross Dress for Less, Dick’s Sporting Goods and Kroger.
“Our investors’ commitments reflect both the strength of open-air retail today and their confidence in how we invest,” said Yoel Mayerfeld , co-chief executive officer of Chase Properties.
“The best centers are in high demand, and pricing reflects that. We’ve owned shopping centers through a lot of cycles since this company was founded more than 50 years ago, and that experience has taught us to be patient and disciplined.”
The fund closings come amid favorable supply and demand fundamentals in the open-air retail sector.
According to Colliers, shopping center vacancy stood at 5.4% in the third quarter of 2026, near historic lows, while CoStar reported that retail construction starts had fallen to their lowest level in at least a decade.
Chase Properties continues to target individual shopping centers and portfolios anchored by national, value-oriented and creditworthy tenants, particularly in secondary and tertiary U.S. markets.
“Our partnership with Tru Arrow has expanded what we can pursue and how quickly we can execute,” said Andy Kline , co-chief executive officer of Chase Properties.
“With both funds closed, we’re actively acquiring, and we want to be the first call from a seller or their broker.”
Glenn Fuhrman , co-founder of Tru Arrow Partners, highlighted Chase Properties’ extensive experience investing in smaller cities and regional markets.
“Having a strong GP that invests its own capital alongside its LPs was a key factor in our investors’ decision to commit to TACPP,” added James Rothschild, co-founder of Tru Arrow Partners.
Founded in 1973, Chase Properties is a vertically integrated real estate investment firm managing more than $1 billion in assets, including approximately eight million square feet of retail space across more than 25 states.
The company primarily invests in open-air shopping centers, with additional investments in multifamily and industrial properties.
Founded in 2021, Tru Arrow Partners is a New York-based investment firm focused on technology and real estate investments, managing capital on behalf of a global network of privately held conglomerates, family offices and other long-term investors.
The combined fund closings provide Chase Properties and Tru Arrow Partners with additional capital to expand their commercial real estate portfolios, with open-air shopping centers remaining a primary investment focus.

Harbinger Secures More Than $100 Million in Debt Financing from Erebor Bank and Pinegrove Venture Partners to Support Production Ramp and Future Growth
News provided by
Harbinger
Nov 24, 2026, 11:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
The combined capital was provided through term loan, revolving debt and convertible note financings to support Harbinger's next stage of growth
GARDEN GROVE, Calif. , Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Harbinger , an American industrial technology platform company, today announced it has closed financing agreements totaling more than $100 million with Erebor Bank , co-founded by Palmer Luckey , and Pinegrove Venture Partners , which is sponsored by Brookfield Asset Management and HRTG Partners. The complementary financing structures include senior debt provided by Erebor and a separate convertible note from Pinegrove.
Continue Reading
Harbinger has secured more than $100 million in financing from Erebor Bank and Pinegrove Venture Partners to accelerate production and support its growing commercial vehicle business.
The transactions mark an important step in Harbinger's evolution from an electric vehicle manufacturer to a broader industrial technology platform company reinventing the critical systems the world depends on across mobility, power, defense, autonomy and components. Harbinger develops advanced electrification technologies, including all-electric and hybrid medium-duty vehicle platforms, battery and drivetrain systems, energy storage and auxiliary power solutions, autonomous driving technology and defense applications.
Harbinger is now scaling production and fulfilling major commercial orders, including its recent multi-year order for 2,000 all-electric trucks from FedEx . Harbinger has added 400 jobs this year, primarily at its Orange County, California headquarters, and plans to continue rapid growth next year, with the goal of creating hundreds of additional jobs around the country.
"Erebor finances companies building the future of American industry—businesses that are making real products, building factories, and scaling U.S. manufacturing," said Palmer Luckey . "Traditional lenders have struggled to support the unique capital needs of businesses developing real technology and scaling domestic jobs. Harbinger is exactly the kind of business we built Erebor to back: an American manufacturer building world-class technology. We're proud to provide the capital to help build more of America's industrial future here at home."
The debt financing comes on the heels of Harbinger's recently announced Series D funding round, and represents an expansion beyond the equity-driven funding model Harbinger has historically utilized as an emerging technology company. By accessing financing structures more commonly associated with established industrial manufacturers, Harbinger is building a more diversified capital strategy to support long-term growth while demonstrating how a new generation of American manufacturers can finance production at scale.
"Building an industrial technology company at scale requires a different financing approach," said John Harris , Co-Founder and CEO, Harbinger. "The capital needed to ramp production and deliver vehicles to customers shouldn't have to come entirely from equity. Major vehicle and aerospace manufacturers have long relied on debt financing to support their production operations, and we're bringing that same approach to Harbinger. Erebor is now our primary banking partner, and together with Pinegrove, they're helping us build the financial foundation to support our next stage of growth."
Erebor is a nationally chartered bank financing the companies rebuilding American industry. Erebor serves customers across 43 states, including businesses in manufacturing, defense, energy, AI, robotics, and aerospace, industries critical to America's national security and economic growth. Built on modern technology, regulated by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), and a member of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), Erebor has grown to $8 billion in assets by expanding access to capital for businesses historically underserved by legacy banks.
"Harbinger is building an impressive industrial technology platform, and we're excited to partner with John and the team as they enter their next phase of growth," said Jim Ellison , Head of Credit, Pinegrove. "Our flexible convertible structure was designed around the company's capital needs and provides Harbinger with additional resources to continue scaling production and investing behind the significant opportunity ahead."
Pinegrove operates as an integrated investment platform with over $15B of assets under management across venture fund primaries, venture and growth secondaries, and private credit. Its private credit strategy provides financing solutions to growth-stage companies, including businesses with significant capital requirements. Its participation in this transaction introduces an additional source of flexible financing for Harbinger as the company expands production, builds manufacturing capacity and pursues new commercial opportunities.
About Harbinger
Harbinger is an American industrial technology platform company reinventing the critical systems the world depends on across mobility, power, defense, autonomy and components. The company develops advanced electrification technologies, including all-electric and hybrid medium-duty vehicle platforms, battery and drivetrain systems, energy storage and auxiliary power solutions, autonomous driving technology and defense applications.
Harbinger engineers systems from first principles, using deep vertical integration to design safer, more reliable, more capable and more efficient solutions at economic parity. Its technologies serve a range of applications, including medium-duty trucks, recreational vehicles (RVs), mobile healthcare units, power infrastructure and defense vehicles. candidates.text:
Yreka Western Railroad Secures $60.2 Million Federal Grant for California Freight Modernization
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:23 PM
Yreka Western Railroad Secures $60.2 Million Federal Grant for California Freight Modernization
Yreka Western Railroad has received a $60.2 million federal grant to modernize its freight corridor between Yreka and Montague in Northern California.
The award was made through the Federal Railroad Administration’s fiscal 2025–2026 Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements program.
Parent company Railmark Holdings is contributing another $20.2 million in cash and in-kind support, bringing the project’s total value to approximately $80.4 million.
Upgrading the Freight Corridor
The project will upgrade the railroad from FRA Excepted Track to Class 2 standards and allow the route to accommodate industry-standard railcars weighing up to 286,000 pounds.
Work will renew 8.43 miles of mainline and approximately 1.5 miles of sidings and industrial spurs. Improvements include new rail, crossties, ballast and other materials, along with the replacement of 21 turnouts.
Two mainline connections will also be built for the separately developed 58-acre Yreka Rail Industrial Park. The project will redeck the Oregon Slough and Shasta River bridges, replace two short-span bridges with culverts and improve four public road crossings in Yreka.
The upgraded infrastructure is expected to support agricultural producers, lumber and forest-products businesses, fertilizer suppliers, propane distributors, recyclers and building-materials shippers.
Yreka Western connects with Union Pacific Railroad and Central Oregon & Pacific Railroad, providing access to the national freight network. Railmark acquired the historic short-line railroad in 2017.
The project was among 105 selected from 368 applications seeking a combined $12.2 billion in federal support.

SenseNet Raises $43 Million to Expand Wildfire Detection
The Series B financing led by Idealist Capital will fund international growth and commercial team expansion for the wildfire monitoring company.
Updated on Nov. 24, 2026 in Startups
SenseNet has secured $43 million in Series B financing led by Idealist Capital, with participation from Fusion Fund, Stormbreaker Ventures, Thin Line Capital, NBC, and The Sitka Foundation. The company said it will use the capital to scale its international operations and grow its commercial teams.
Why it matters
The financing supports expansion of wildfire monitoring as the company reports tripling its global footprint from 130 million to more than 450 million acres over the last year. The round is expected to accelerate SenseNet's growth in the US and internationally as wildfire risks intensify.
SenseNet's $43 million Series B round includes primary and secondary sales plus debt financing, while its network has grown to more than 5,300 sensors and AI-enabled cameras across 12 countries. The company has not disclosed the proportion of each financing type or its valuation.
The players
SenseNet
SenseNet is a wildfire detection company that deploys sensors, AI-enabled cameras and predictive analytics across multiple countries.
Idealist Capital
Idealist Capital is an investment firm that led the Series B financing round for SenseNet.
The details
SenseNet combines ground-level environmental sensors, AI-enabled cameras, satellite intelligence, drone technology, and predictive analytics into one multimodal ecosystem that integrates with existing third-party and emergency systems without replacing current infrastructure. The company reports US customers including Palo Alto and Woodside fire departments, Santa Clara County and San Jose Water in California, and Jefferson County and the City of Colorado Springs in Colorado.
Timeline
Over the last year: SenseNet tripled its global wildfire monitoring footprint.
During the past wildfire season: SenseNet detected several fires hours before the first 911 reports.
November 24, 2026: SenseNet announced the $43 million Series B financing.
Market Landscape
SenseNet's multimodal approach, which layers ground sensors, AI cameras, satellite intelligence and drones, extends the AI-enabled camera and satellite wildfire detection systems now used by fire departments and water utilities. Its ability to integrate with existing emergency systems positions it as an add-on to current infrastructure rather than a replacement.
Fire departments and water utilities in California, Colorado and other customer regions may gain earlier wildfire alerts through SenseNet's integrated systems. The extraction does not indicate any change to pricing or availability for residents.
The takeaway
Wildfire detection is increasingly being built as layered systems that connect with existing emergency services, which may help agencies respond sooner as fire seasons lengthen.

candidates.text:
Global , South Florida

Native Realty Brokers $35.38 Million Sale of Gateway Shopping District in Fort Lauderdale
November 24, 2026
CEO Jaime Sturgis unites several property owners to close 11-building, 73,756-square-foot retail sale to Miami-based CORE
Native Realty , the Fort Lauderdale-based firm led by Jaime Sturgis , closed the $35.38 million sale of Gateway Shopping District, a 73,756-square-foot retail district located at 1900 E. Sunrise Blvd . in Fort Lauderdale. Miami-based CORE acquired the property.
Native CEO Jaime Sturgis represented the seller, and Native Associate Jeremiah Adler represented the buyer. The transaction closed on Nov. 20.
The sale includes 11 buildings. Only the building at 1990 E. Sunrise Blvd . was excluded from the transaction.
Gateway’s sale marks the culmination of Sturgis’ long-term efforts to revitalize the site through adaptive reuse and thoughtful tenant curation. Gateway was a fractured retail site, with different individual owners holding different buildings within the overall property.
To bring the transaction across the finish line, Sturgis had to secure each individual seller and reconcile differing motivations, timelines and aspirations. He worked to align the group and cross-collateralize the properties so the sale could move forward as a single transaction.
Jeremiah Adler and Jaime Sturgis
“Gateway has always been a site with enormous potential, but its ownership structure made a sale of this scale extremely complicated,” Sturgis said. “Our job was to listen, build trust and find a path that worked for everyone. Seeing this property transform from a neglected shopping center into one of the most dynamic retail destinations in Fort Lauderdale, and then closing a sale of this size, is incredibly rewarding.”
Gateway’s history spans several eras. The site began as a quarry and rockyard before being converted into Jungle Zoo in 1940. It was later redeveloped as a supermarket, then a big-box retail center and, most recently, a boutique neighborhood plaza.
Prior to Native being hired more than five years ago to lease and manage the property, Gateway languished for several decades and accumulated significant deferred maintenance. The center needed new roofs, windows, doors, fixtures, flooring, painting, facades and much more. Native balanced overseeing the complete rehabilitation of the center with simultaneously launching a leasing campaign to attract new tenants.
Sturgis and the Native team reimagined Gateway with a bustling mix of food-and-beverage and experiential retailers, creating a modern retail district that takes full advantage of the site’s highly visible and prime location.
Gateway sits very close to the Galleria Mall, where developer Russell Galbut and his partners are embarking on a major mixed-use redevelopment that will transform the mall into an eight-building destination.
The sale serves as a case study in how Native draws on its vast local market knowledge and relationships to activate a long-dormant asset and position it for a successful exit for the property owner.
About Native Realty: Founded in 2017 by Fort Lauderdale-based commercial real estate broker Jaime Sturgis, Native Realty’s experienced commercial real estate professionals specializes in investment sales and leasing across the region’s urban core and emerging markets, advising institutional investors, private capital groups, developers and owner-operators on high-stakes acquisitions and dispositions. The firm recently surpassed $1 billion in overall transaction volume and generated more than $350 million in 2025 volume. Native moved up eight spots in the South Florida Business Journal’s 2026 Commercial Real Estate Brokerages ranking, which is based on the previous year’s transaction volume. The firm is also widely recognized for its role in shaping Fort Lauderdale’s Flagler Village, where it has completed several million square feet in transactions.
Native continues to grow strategically by adding senior commercial real estate brokers who align with its collaborative, high-performance culture. The firm offers a platform where top producers can expand their businesses, leverage a connected team and compete at the highest level of the South Florida market. Native serves clients of every size, from Fortune 500 companies to small businesses. Native is headquartered at 1926 E. Sunrise Blvd . in Fort Lauderdale. For more information, visit www.nativerealty.com .

candidates.title: Prosus to lead Rs 38 crore funding in Vegapay as fintech bets gather pace
candidates.snippet: Prosus to lead Rs 38 crore funding in Vegapay as fintech bets gather pace The Economic Times
candidates.text:
Synopsis
Prosus will invest Rs 28.8 crore through its investment arm, while Elevation Capital, Vertex Ventures and Eximius Ventures will put in Rs 6 crore, Rs 2.3 crore and Rs 1.3 crore, respectively, according to filings with the Registrar of Companies.
Listen to this article in summarized format Listen
ETtech (L-R) Abhinav Garg, Himanshu Agrawal, Puneet Sharma and Gaurav Mittal, founders, Vegapay
Amsterdam-listed technology investor Prosus is set to lead a Rs 38.4 crore funding round in fintech infrastructure startup Vegapay , with participation from existing investors Elevation Capital, Vertex Ventures and Eximius Ventures.
Prosus will invest Rs 28.8 crore through its investment arm, while Elevation Capital, Vertex Ventures and Eximius Ventures will put in Rs 6 crore, Rs 2.3 crore and Rs 1.3 crore, respectively, according to filings with the Registrar of Companies.
The investment will value the Mumbai-based startup at about Rs 380 crore ($38-40 million) post-money, according to the share issuance details. Prosus will hold a 7.6% stake in the company, while Elevation Capital will own 25.1%.
The proposed investment comes just months after Vegapay raised Rs 37.9 crore from its existing investors in a round led by Vertex Ventures. People aware of the matter said the latest share issuance is part of a larger funding round. Entrackr first reported the proposed share issuance.
The deal marks an expansion of Prosus' fintech investment portfolio beyond companies directly offering credit and other financial products to those building the underlying technology infrastructure for financial institutions.
ET reported earlier this month that Prosus, which has invested $100 million in the Sachin Bansal-founded Navi, around $80 million in supply-chain financing platform Mintifi and $100 million in Vastu Housing Finance over the past two years, is looking to increase its exposure to financial services after years of backing consumer internet companies in India.
“You will see us over-indexing on financial services,” Ashutosh Sharma, head of India investments at Prosus, had told ET, pointing to opportunities where technology can expand access to financial products or improve the economics of delivering them.
Prosus was also close to investing in artificial intelligence-led credit management startup Oolka, ET had reported.
Founded in 2022 by Gaurav Mittal, Himanshu Agrawal, Puneet Sharma and Abhinav Garg, Vegapay develops software for banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) to launch and manage credit products without having to overhaul their existing technology systems.
Its offerings include card issuance and management, credit lines on the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), as well as software for loan origination, colending and collections. It competes with rivals such as SoftBank-backed banking technology startup Zeta.
Vegapay had raised $5.5 million in May 2024 in a round led by Elevation Capital. Its operating revenue grew nearly threefold to Rs 8.7 crore in FY26, while the net loss widened marginally to Rs 18.7 crore.
